method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.title: Stocks inch up as oil weighed by supply while earnings loom
Equities.reason: Broad market note ahead of earnings—modest risk-on tone as stocks edge higher; useful snapshot of near-term market positioning ahead of earnings week.

Equities.title: Big investors commit billions to private credit despite turmoil
Equities.summary: Institutional investors poured money into funds as retail money fled
Equities.reason: Flows into private credit imply some capital is shifting away from public equities/liquidity pools—a modest headwind for broad equity risk appetite.

Equities.title: Morgan Stanley’s Wilson Sees Rotation From Chips to Hyperscalers
Equities.reason: Indicates intra-tech rotation rather than broad sell-off—supports a narrative of sector leadership shifting within tech (AI compute suppliers vs. cloud hyperscalers).

Equities.title: Nvidia AI Server Delay Report Sends Asian PCB Stocks Sliding
Equities.reason: Product/production delays at a major AI supplier are a negative for chip supply-chain names and chip-driven equity momentum; increases downside risk for tech leadership.

Equities.title: Samsung likely to post 18-fold jump in profit on surging AI demand for memory
Equities.reason: Very strong earnings preview for a major memory supplier reinforces AI-led earnings upside and supports chip-equity leadership — significant positive signal for tech/AI narrative.

Equities.title: Stalled AI Rally Has More Eyeing Old-Guard Stocks
Equities.reason: Signals a cooling of the AI-momentum trade and rotation back to cyclical/value names — negative for momentum/AI leadership but mixed for broader market depending on breadth.

Equities.title: Why the stock market’s red-hot momentum trade might be headed for a violent unwind this month
Equities.reason: Highlights concentrated momentum risk and potential for a sharp de-risking—meaningful negative tail-risk for equity indices dominated by momentum names.

Equities.title: Record wave of IPO lock-up shares to hit Hong Kong market
Equities.reason: Large scheduled lock-up expiries in Hong Kong imply potential selling pressure and volatility for HK/China equities; negative for regional risk sentiment.

Equities.title: Trump's calls, Ukraine's strikes and Russia's barrage on Kyiv put markets on alert
Equities.summary: Trump reportedly spoke with Putin and Zelenskyy as Ukraine struck Russian targets and Moscow launched another deadly attack on Kyiv.
Equities.reason: Escalating geopolitical headlines increase risk-off pressures and could weigh on global risk assets and sectoral cyclicals; meaningful for near-term sentiment.

Equities.title: SK Hynix Seeks Access to AI Investors in $29 Billion US Listing
Equities.reason: Large AI-linked listing would deepen AI-related equity supply/demand dynamics and reflects continued investor appetite for AI exposure — modestly positive for tech sentiment.

Equities.title: Wall Street sees more upside in stocks for second half of 2026
Equities.reason: Broad bullish analyst/strategist outlook supports a constructive regime view for equities into H2 — positive for sentiment and positioning, though forward-looking.

Rates.title: US Dollar: Services data guide Fed expectations – BNY
Rates.summary: BNY’s Geoff Yu highlights that softer U.S. labor data and easing inflation have reduced pressure for further Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening, but upcoming US Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) and ISM Services will be crucial for rate expectations.
Rates.reason: Softer US labour and easing inflation cited as reducing Fed tightening pressure — dovish repricing supportive for US bonds (yields down / bond rally). Services data are the next risk to this view.

Rates.title: New Zealand Dollar: RBNZ set for further tightening – BNY
Rates.summary: BNY’s Geoff Yu expects the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) to raise the Official Cash Rate (OCR) by 25bp to 2.50%, supported by stronger Gross Domestic Product (GDP), resilient labor markets and firm inflation near the top of target.
Rates.reason: Expectations of a 25bp RBNZ hike imply tighter NZ monetary policy and higher local yields (bond-selloff locally); limited global spill but relevant for NZ rates markets.

Rates.title: Bond Traders Watch for Treasury Auctions, June Fed Minutes
Rates.reason: Focus on Treasury supply (auctions) and Fed minutes raises risk of higher yields/volatility if demand softens or minutes signal persistence of tighter policy — negative for bond prices.

Rates.title: Isabel Schnabel: Is inflation back?
Rates.reason: ECB official questioning whether inflation is resurging points to upside risks to price pressures and persistence of ECB hawkishness — pressure on European bond prices / higher yields.

Rates.title: Indian rupee to track merchant flows, dollar; bonds await foreign buying cues
Rates.reason: Headline highlights that Indian government bonds are sensitive to foreign buying flows — potential supportive flow into bonds if buying materialises (mildly positive for Indian yields/bonds).

FX.title: Australian Dollar drifts away from highs amid cooler inflation, weak employment data
FX.summary: The Australian Dollar (AUD) is trading moderately lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, as cooler Australian inflation figures have eased pressure on the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to hike interest rates further.
FX.reason: Domestic Australian data (cooler inflation, weak jobs) reduces RBA hawkishness and feeds USD strength. Clear USD-led pressure on AUD — moderate relevance for USD-centric FX narrative.

FX.title: Indonesian Rupiah weakens as Fed hike bets lift US Dollar
FX.summary: USD/IDR rises for the second successive day, trading around 18,040 during the Asian hours on Monday. The pair appreciates as the US Dollar receives support from prevailing market expectations of Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hikes later this year.
FX.reason: Explicit link to Fed hike expectations lifting the USD and pressuring EMFX (IDR). Strong USD driver with direct FX transmission — high relevance for USD-EMFX flows.

FX.title: US Dollar Index: Upside risks stay supported – ING
FX.summary: ING’s Chris Turner notes the Dollar (USD) has held up after soft June jobs data, with G7 FX volatility low and carry trades attractive as one-week Dollar deposit rates sit in the upper G10 range.
FX.reason: Analyst view that structural carry and deposit-rate advantage support the DXY — clear market-level USD strength narrative with broad FX implications (high relevance).

FX.title: Swiss Franc declines as US Dollar rebounds, eyes on US Services PMI
FX.summary: The Swiss Franc (CHF) faces selling pressure against the US Dollar (USD) at the start of the week. The USD/CHF pair is down 0.25% to near 0.8055 during the European trading session as the US Dollar rebounds despite traders reconsidering Federal Reserve (Fed) i
FX.reason: Direct USD rebound versus CHF; short-term USD strength story tied to US data/Pricing of Fed policy — medium relevance to G10 FX moves.

FX.title: Euro: ECB support offsets Dollar strength – Commerzbank
FX.summary: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister argues that recent EUR/USD weakness reflects a stronger US Dollar (USD) rather than a fundamentally weak Euro (EUR), as the Euro has outperformed the G10 average.
FX.reason: Acknowledges USD-driven EUR weakness but highlights ECB support as a partial offset — signals USD pressure but with an important regional counterbalance (moderate relevance).

FX.title: United States Dollar Index rises to near 101.00 on Fed hikes this year
FX.summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the value of the US Dollar (USD) against six major currencies, is gaining ground after remaining unchanged in the previous day and trading around 101.00 during the Asian hours on Monday.
FX.reason: Plain DXY move higher tied to Fed hikes — broad market signal of USD strength that drives most G10/EM FX moves (high relevance).

FX.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Eyes 40-year highs near 163.00 after breaking above nine-day EMA
FX.summary: USD/JPY gains ground for the second successive day, trading around 162.20 during the early European hours on Monday. The currency pair is maintaining a bullish near-term bias as it holds comfortably above both the nine-day and 50-day Exponential Moving Average
FX.reason: Technical/price-forecast piece showing a strong USD vs JPY move toward multi-decade highs — signals USD dominance vs major funding currency (technical relevance capped).

FX.title: Japanese Yen declines towards 162.00 vs USD as carry trades counter intervention risks
FX.summary: The USD/JPY pair builds on its goodish recovery from the 160.50-160.45 region, or over a two-week low touched on Friday, and gains strong follow-through traction for the second straight day on Monday.
FX.reason: Describes carry-driven USD/JPY move higher; highlights the tension between market carry flows and intervention risk — strong USD flow signal into JPY (high relevance).

FX.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks shape Dollar pullback – MUFG
FX.summary: MUFG’s Teppei Ino reviews recent USD/JPY price action, noting the pair opened near 161.78 and briefly tested the 162.84 area before reversing. The report highlights Dollar weakness after comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and a softer US employment report.
FX.reason: Highlights intervention risk and recent USD softness vs JPY after Fed comments and softer US jobs — a credible counter-signal to the prevailing USD-strong move (lower-medium relevance).

FX.title: Indian Rupee declines against US Dollar at the start of FOMC Minutes week
FX.summary: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades lower against the US Dollar (USD) at the start of the week.
FX.reason: Simple USD-led INR depreciation at start of FOMC minutes week — direct USD-EMFX transmission with modest relevance.

FX.title: Carry Traders Shift Away From Dollar for Emerging-Market Bets
FX.reason: Title indicates a flow shift away from the USD into EM carry — if sustained this is a meaningful thematic counterweight to USD strength and important for EMFX positioning (high relevance).

FX.title: South Korea starts 24-hour trading of dollar-won
FX.reason: Market-structure change increasing USD/KRW trading hours and liquidity. Not a direct directional USD shock but affects FX market functioning and potential intraday flows (modest relevance).

FX.title: Yen pinned near 40-year lows as intervention risks mount
FX.reason: Headline points to USD/JPY at multi-decade lows for JPY (i.e., USD strength) with intervention risk — reinforces major USD-vs-JPY dominance and market intervention narrative (high relevance).

Commodities.title: Oil: Diverging market paths under geopolitical camps – Rabobank
Commodities.summary: Rabobank’s Senior Market Strategist Benjamin Picton highlights that Brent has turned lower as OPEC+ eases production cuts and tanker flows through the Strait of Hormuz resume, but stresses that shipping risks remain crucial for Oil prices.
Commodities.reason: Analyst view flags easing OPEC+ discipline and resumed Hormuz flows — both increase supply / reduce risk premium. Negative for oil prices; analyst note is market-relevant but not breaking news, so medium relevance.

Commodities.title: Oil slips after OPEC+ agrees to raise output targets
Commodities.reason: Direct report that OPEC+ is raising output targets is a clear supply-side increase and a near-term headwind for oil prices. High relevance given market-moving policy from producers.

Commodities.title: OPEC+ Ratifies Planned Oil Quota Hike as Gulf Flows Rebound
Commodities.reason: Bloomberg confirms OPEC+ quota hikes and rebound in Gulf flows — reinforces the dominant supply story that should weigh on prices. High relevance as it corroborates producer actions and shipping changes.

Commodities.title: Why Iran may find it difficult to clear its oil inventories even after sanctions relief
Commodities.summary: Iran may face challenges in clearing oil inventories even after restrictions have been lifted, amid oil supplies elsewhere while China becomes less enthusiastic
Commodities.reason: Article highlights potential persistent inventories from Iran and weaker Chinese demand appetite — net surplus risk to the market. Moderately relevant as it adds to the oversupply narrative.

Commodities.title: U.S. refining capacity decreased during 2025
Commodities.summary: U.S. operable atmospheric distillation capacity, the primary measure of refinery capacity, totaled 18.2 million barrels per calendar day (b/cd) on January 1, 2026-down over 250,000 b/cd (about 1%) compared with January 1, 2025-according to our latest annual Re
Commodities.reason: Lower U.S. refining capacity reduces product-side throughput and can support crude and refined product prices; directly relevant fundamental supply-side datapoint with medium relevance.

Commodities.title: Gold prices set for first weekly rise in a month as investors scale back Fed rate hike bets
Commodities.summary: The metal was boosted as investors scaled back their bets on a looming rate hike.
Commodities.reason: Slower Fed tightening expectations reduce real yields and boost gold demand — clear positive macro driver for gold with above-average relevance.

Commodities.title: China’s Biggest ETF Is Now a Gold Fund as National Team Retreats
Commodities.reason: Major shift in China ETF composition signals a large structural bid for gold from Asia / institutional flows. High directional impact and high relevance for the global gold market.

Commodities.title: Gold Steadies After Weekly Gain as Rate-Hike Worries Recede
Commodities.reason: Reinforces the prevailing precious-metals narrative that fading rate-hike fears are supportive for gold; medium-high relevance as market-confirming color.

Commodities.title: Gold hangs near daily low as Hormuz risks support USD; receding Fed hike bets limit losses
Commodities.summary: Gold (XAU/USD) recovers slightly from the daily low, albeit it retains the negative bias through the first half of the European session and remains below a two-week high touched earlier this Monday.
Commodities.reason: Intraday/technical note tying gold action to a stronger USD and Hormuz-related flows. Price-forecast/technical story — lower relevance and small negative directional tilt.

Commodities.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD holds losses below $62.50 on Fed hike bets
Commodities.summary: Silver price (XAG/USD) halts its four-day winning streak, trading around $62.30 per troy ounce during the European hours on Monday. The white metal edges lower as market expectations solidify around a Federal Reserve (Fed) interest rate hike later this year.
Commodities.reason: Silver is sensitive to real rates and Fed expectations; this is a short-term price-forecast/technical piece so relevance is capped but direction is moderately negative given firmer Fed-hike bets.

Commodities.title: Copper and Aluminum Advance on Fading Expectations for Rate Hike
Commodities.reason: Weaker rate-hike expectations lift industrial metals demand/price via lower real yields and macro-support for growth; copper is in the 1XW universe so this is a meaningful positive signal with above-average relevance.
